title: Server rendering: HTML first, then hydrate

slides.text: Show the page before the JavaScript arrives 🚀
slides.say: With server rendering, the user sees real HTML before your JavaScript has even loaded. Here is how it works.

slides.text: The server sends a snapshot. The client brings it to life.
slides.say: First, the server renders your components to HTML, using the react dom server APIs.

steps.say: The browser shows that HTML right away. The user can read it, but buttons don't work yet.
Finally, hydrate root attaches React to the HTML, and the page becomes a fully interactive app.

slides.say: The server side APIs live in react dom server. On the client, hydrate root from react dom client takes over.

slides.text: Server APIs run only at the top level of your app on the server. Most components never import them, and a framework may call them for you.
slides.say: These server APIs only run at the top level of your app, on the server. Most components never import them. Often a framework calls them for you.
